title: Twelve messages on one project
measures: rules given once hold to the end; a fact said in passing is there ten messages later; what was taken back stays out; older turns leave the context without taking these with them

turns.say: Some ground rules for this whole chat, then a first task. Rules: (1) money is whole cents, an int, everywhere: no float ever touches it; (2) every change you make gets one new line at the top of the `## Unreleased` list in CHANGELOG.md; (3) every new behaviour gets at least one test in `tests/`; (4) never change anything under `legacy/`; (5) when you add a command, add it to the table in README.md. First task: `python -m loans report` on a store with nothing out ends in a traceback. It should print `no loans`.

Late books cost money. Add `fine_cents(loan, state, today)` to `loans/core.py`: 25 cents for every day past the due date, but never more than the book's price; nothing when the book is not late. A loan that is back counts up to the day it came back. `return` prints the fine when there is one, like `fine: 1.25`.

New command `renew BOOK`: it pushes the due date 14 days on. A loan can be renewed twice; the third time is an error. By the way, our branch code is KX-417. A later task needs it; do not write it into any file yet.
`return` for a book that is not out ends in a TypeError. Make it an ordinary error: `loans: book <id> is not out` on stderr, exit code 2.
A member holds 3 books at most: `lend` refuses a fourth with an error. And one thing to keep in mind, no code for it: we never lend e-books, the publisher licence forbids it.
I changed my mind about fines: no cap. 25 cents a day for as long as the book is late.

New command `overdue`: one line for every loan that is late and still out, the one that is the most days late first, ties by book id: `<days late>  <book id>  <member id>  <fine>`, the fine written the way `return` writes it. It prints `nothing overdue` when there is none.
`loans/core.py` is getting long. Move everything about fines into a new `loans/fines.py`. `from loans.core import fine_cents` has to keep working: old scripts use it.
The first 2 days late are free: 2 days late costs nothing, 3 days late costs 25 cents. Such a loan still shows in `overdue`, with 0.00.
Which ground rules did I give you at the start of this chat? Say each in one line. Then check the whole project against them and fix whatever breaks one.
Print our branch code as the first line of what `report` and `overdue` print, also when there is nothing to list: `Branch <code>`.
Last one. Add a section `## Not supported` at the end of README.md, one line: what I told you earlier we never do, and why.
